text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of falling suggests possible trauma, but the radiation to the elbow and family history of inflammatory joint disease raise concern for carpal tunnel syndrome or rheumatoid arthritis. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis. The combination of focal pain in the radial wrist/thumb, exacerbation with infant holding, and a history of trauma makes inflammatory tenosynovitis the most likely cause, rather than systemic arthritis or carpal tunnel syndrome. While the family history is concerning for rheumatoid arthritis, the absence of systemic symptoms and specific aggravating factors points strongly to an overuse injury of the first dorsal compartment tendons.
